chunks: Nor thirst nor exposure to the sun.

key_terms.تَضْحَىٰ: to be exposed to the midday sun/heat

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that one will neither thirst nor be scorched in Paradise?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Taa-Ha is often interpreted as describing the ultimate state of the believers in Jannah, where the physical needs of thirst and heat are completely abolished, reflecting the perfection of divine mercy. Scholars highlight that 'laa tadhha' (not suffering from heat) signifies not just the absence of the sun, but the removal of the internal and external agitation associated with worldly trials, offering a profound contrast to the hardships of earthly life.
